weather_report:
As evening settles over Boston, the city envelops itself in a soft blanket of rain and hazy fog, lending the familiar streets a touch of the ethereal. The clouds brood overhead, heavy with moisture and murmuring with the potential for distant thunder. Those venturing outside will find the air cool, around the mid-fifties, a gentle reminder of the season's shift. A light breeze brushes in from the southwest, encouraging a sense of introspection as the droplets gather on leaves, creating a symphony of sound against pavement.

Saturday promises a continuation of this reverie, with the rain expected to linger—albeit reluctantly—with only intermittent breaks in the gloom. The forecast hints at a high near sixty-three, suggesting that while the day will be predominantly overcast, the murky veil might part just enough to reveal the lingering colors of autumn. A mere whisper of a north wind will accompany the day—a subtle contrast against the rain, nudging thoughts toward cozy indoor activities. A good wrap or an umbrella will be your faithful companions if you take to the streets, or perhaps consider a leisurely visit to a local café. There, you might find solace in a warm cup while watching the world glide by, cloaked in mist and mystery.
